shifts.summary: The paper was overall judged moderate, with candidates reporting good attempts between 65 and 82. Reasoning was mostly easy but some found it moderate to difficult, and attempts ranged 17–24. Quantitative aptitude was widely seen as difficult, with time pressure limiting attempts to about 15–20. English was consistently described as easy, focusing on synonym‑antonym and passage items.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Reasoning was described as easy and doable within 10‑11 minutes by some candidates, while others found it moderate to difficult and lengthy.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: General Awareness featured factual GK, current affairs from 2025, and policy questions such as Swachh Bharat, with some candidates finding it easy and others difficult.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Math section had long questions, time pressure of 15 min, candidates could attempt about 15‑16 questions, with many reporting difficulty.

sections.notes: English comprised synonym‑antonym, one‑word substitution, idioms and a passage, and was generally considered easy.

shifts.summary: The shift 3 paper showed mixed difficulty levels across sections. Overall difficulty ranged from Easy to Moderate, with most reports rating it Easy. Reasoning and GA were generally easy, while Quant varied and English was mostly easy. Good attempt counts were between 75 and 84 overall.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Many conclusion type questions, no trigonometry. Moderate level present but easy also noted. Statement‑based and symbol‑related questions were common.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: All 25 GS questions attempted, mainly statistics. Current affairs and GDP questions were also present. Articles and Amendments appeared in some questions.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: 15 minutes for 25 questions, manageable. No DI/DI and fewer advanced questions. Some time‑consuming direct‑formula and graph problems appeared.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: Paragraphs were long but manageable. Vocabulary and voice‑narration questions were asked. Option mismatch questions appeared in Hindi/English.

intro: On 23 October 2026 the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam was taken in three shifts. All three shifts were reported as having a moderate overall difficulty, with shift 3 receiving some easy ratings. Reported good‑attempt counts range from 65 to 84 questions across the shifts, but these figures are unofficial and SSC normalises scores across shifts. Section‑wise feedback shows reasoning generally easy to moderate, quantitative aptitude perceived as difficult to hard, and English largely easy.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty of the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 23 October 2026?
faqs.a: All three shifts on 23 October 2026 were reported as moderate overall, with shift 3 having some reports of easy difficulty.

faqs.q: How did candidates describe the reasoning section on 23 October 2026?
faqs.a: Reasoning was described as mostly easy to moderate across the shifts on 23 October 2026, with a few candidates finding it moderate to difficult.

faqs.q: What was the perceived difficulty of the quantitative aptitude section on 23 October 2026?
faqs.a: Quantitative aptitude was widely seen as difficult on shifts 1 and 2, and ranged from moderate to hard on shift 3 on 23 October 2026.

faqs.q: How many good attempts were reported for the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 23 October 2026?
faqs.a: Reported good‑attempt ranges were 65–82 for shift 1, 65–77 for shift 2, and 75–84 for shift 3 on 23 October 2026. These numbers are unofficial.

faqs.q: How does SSC handle score comparison across shifts for the 23 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: SSC normalises scores across shifts, so the unofficial good‑attempt figures are adjusted to a common scale for final ranking.
